channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Pavlodar Court Cancels Tender for "Cyber Sheriff" System Maintenance
item.description: A court in Pavlodar region has invalidated the tender results for the maintenance and technical support of the "Cyber Sheriff" system for 2026. The winning company submitted falsified certificates of training from a non-existent Dutch institution.

item.title: Spanish University Proposes Campus Construction in Osh, Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Representatives from Spain's Universidad Europea del Atlántico met with Osh city officials to propose building a campus and branch in the southern Kyrgyz capital. The university requested land allocation, and the municipality expressed interest in exploring options.

item.title: Suspects Detained in Balkhash for Forcing Two Sisters, Aged 13 and 15, into Prostitution
item.description: In Balkhash, Kazakhstan, criminal proceedings are underway regarding alleged sexual violence against two teenage sisters, aged 13 and 15. A relative claims the girls were beaten, abused, and forced into prostitution for months. The father stated that the girls were befriended by an older acquaintance who introduced them to her contacts.

item.title: World Bank: Over 15 Million Afghans Face Acute Food Insecurity
item.description: The World Bank reports that 15.9 million people in Afghanistan are experiencing acute food insecurity. Declining purchasing power and rising prices are exacerbating living conditions for families. Daily wage workers faced 14% fewer working days in September compared to last year, and their purchasing power has decreased across all provinces.

item.title: Qatar and UK Representatives Discuss Latest Developments in Afghanistan
item.description: Representatives from Qatar and the United Kingdom have held discussions regarding the most recent developments in Afghanistan. The meeting focused on the current situation and potential future scenarios within the country.

item.title: Uzbek President Orders Daily Oversight of New Tashkent Investment Projects
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has mandated daily oversight for investment projects in the New Tashkent development. He also criticized inaccuracies in the "Yashil Makon" project, emphasizing strict discipline and the removal of barriers for investors.

item.title: Efforts Underway to Deliver Urgent Humanitarian Aid to Needy Afghans
item.description: Efforts are being made to deliver urgent humanitarian aid to Afghans in need. This initiative aims to address the critical needs of the population. Further details on the scope and specifics of the aid delivery are expected.

item.title: New Head Appointed to Kyrgyzstan's Water Resources Service
item.description: Emilbek Zakirov has been appointed as the new director of Kyrgyzstan's Water Resources Service, replacing Baktybek Anarkulov who resigned. The appointment was signed by Cabinet Chairman Adylbek Kasymaliev. Zakirov, a lawyer by education, previously worked in the State Service for Combating Economic Crimes and as an expert in the presidential administration. He is tasked with promptly addressing industry issues.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Italy Discuss Expanding Air Service
item.description: Kazakhstan and Italy held talks on expanding air connectivity, including potential new routes for an Italian airline to Atyrau. Discussions focused on civil aviation cooperation, new technologies, digitalization, and sustainable air transport. Both sides expressed interest in increasing flights to boost tourism and economic ties.

item.title: Proposal to Erect Monument to Jusup Abdrakhmanov in Kazakhstan
item.description: A scientific conference in Almaty proposed erecting a monument to Jusup Abdrakhmanov, former chairman of the Council of People's Commissars of the Kirghiz ASSR, in either Almaty or Astana. Kazakhstani scientists suggested this initiative to honor his role in saving Kazakh refugees and to commemorate Kyrgyz-Kazakh brotherhood.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Ban Privatization of Green Zones Near Schools and Hospitals
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to prohibit the privatization of green zones and other lands within state educational and medical institutions by January 20, 2027. This measure is part of broader programs focusing on environmental protection and water resource management, including promoting water-saving technologies in agriculture.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Kurultai Approves Budget and Minimum Wage Increase to 110,000 Tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Kurultai has approved the republican budget for 2027-2029, including a minimum wage increase from 85,000 to 110,000 tenge starting January 1, 2027. The budget allocates funds for various initiatives, including healthcare worker salaries and AI in schools.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Abolish Employer Bank Link for Salary Payments
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank announced the upcoming abolition of mandatory salary payments through the employer's bank. Employees will soon be able to receive salaries on cards or e-wallets of their choice, with employers submitting a unified payment registry. This aims to enhance convenience and competition.

item.title: Taliban Leader Declares End to Religious Diversity in Afghanistan
item.description: Taliban leader Hibatullah Akhundzada stated that engaging with followers of the Shafi'i school of Islamic jurisprudence is unacceptable. He claimed all Afghan citizens now follow the Hanafi school, asserting an end to religious diversity. The Afghanistan Islamic Unity Party criticized these remarks as contrary to historical realities and denying the identities of a portion of the population.

item.title: Canada Funds Women's Rights and Development Projects in Uzbekistan
item.description: The Canadian Embassy in Uzbekistan is funding local non-governmental organizations through the Canadian Fund for Local Initiatives. Grants range from $20,000 to $100,000 CAD, supporting projects focused on women's rights, inclusive governance, human rights, and sustainable development. Past projects include supporting women's participation in the labor market and combating gender discrimination.

item.title: Erdogan Urges Muslim Countries to Act on Gaza Crisis, Increase Pressure on Israel
item.description: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan called on Muslim countries not to remain silent in the face of the humanitarian catastrophe in Gaza. He emphasized the importance of sending humanitarian aid to the region and stressed the need to increase pressure on Israel. The statement was made during a call for action regarding the ongoing conflict.

item.title: Kazakhstan Advocates for Consolidated International Efforts Against Terrorism
item.description: Kazakhstan's Foreign Minister Mukhtar Tileuberdi participated in the Shuman Forum on Security and Defense, speaking on the evolving nature of terrorist threats. He highlighted challenges like radical ideologies online, cross-border extremism, and risks to critical infrastructure. Tileuberdi stressed the need for coordinated international action, including information exchange and best practices.

item.title: Protests Erupt in Iran After 13 Oil Workers Die in Road Accident
item.description: Residents of Abadan in western Iran protested on November 17 following the deaths of 13 oil and gas sector workers in a road accident. At least seven people were detained by security forces. Protesters demanded accountability for the accident and the resignation of officials, with some chanting anti-government slogans.

item.title: China's 9th CIIE Exhibition Supports Asia-Pacific Development and Global Trade
item.description: The 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE) opened in Shanghai, offering global companies access to the Chinese market. The exhibition serves as a model for regional cooperation and aims to foster an Asia-Pacific community. Despite rising protectionism, CIIE highlights the region's economic growth and commitment to shared prosperity.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Legal Literacy Program in All Schools by 2031
item.description: Uzbekistan will introduce a legal literacy program in all general education schools by 2031, according to a presidential decree. The program aims to strengthen the rule of law and will include lessons on rights, protection from violence, labor, and consumer rights. Teacher training and methodological materials will be developed.

item.title: Foreign Entrepreneurs Increasingly Choose Khorgos as a Trade Hub
item.description: The Chinese city of Khorgos is becoming a land of opportunity for entrepreneurs from Central Asia and Europe. Once a stop on ancient trade routes, it's now a key point of China's openness to the west. Improvements in customs processing have facilitated faster trade, especially for perishable goods.

item.title: Uzbekistan Plans $5 Billion Investment in Karakalpakstan's Development
item.description: Uzbekistan is set to invest $5 billion in Karakalpakstan by 2027 to accelerate economic and social development in the region, which faces environmental challenges from the Aral Sea's drying. The plan aims to double investment, increase exports to $550 million, and boost regional economy by 8%.

item.title: Kazakhstan Leads Central Asia in Innovation Development, Ranks 73rd Globally
item.description: Kazakhstan has climbed eight places to 73rd out of 139 countries in the Global Innovation Index 2026, leading Central Asia. The Ministry of Science and Higher Education reported improvements in high-tech exports and production complexity. A new innovation development concept for 2026-2030 has been approved.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Data Center Electricity Pricing Debate Relevant to Kyrgyzstan
item.description: A debate in Kazakhstan over electricity prices for data centers, with an expert suggesting selling power at 2.5 cents per kilowatt-hour is unprofitable, holds relevance for Kyrgyzstan. If Kazakhstan adopts a 'replacement cost' pricing of 6.5-7.5 cents, it could impact Kyrgyzstan's energy imports from Kazakhstan.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Rangers Receive Spotting Scopes for Snow Leopard Monitoring
item.description: Rangers in Kyrgyzstan have received three spotting scopes to aid in monitoring snow leopards and their prey. The equipment, donated by the Bishkek Snow Leopard Run organizers, will be deployed in key reserves. This initiative aims to improve wildlife observation and anti-poaching efforts.

item.title: Tashkent Welcomes International Judo Federation President for Youth Championships
item.description: Marius Vizer, President of the International Judo Federation, has arrived in Tashkent to attend the Youth World Championships. The event, starting tomorrow, will feature nearly 600 athletes from 82 countries competing until November 22nd.

item.title: Uzbekistan Shares Public Administration Reforms Experience in China
item.description: Uzbekistan presented its public administration reform experience at an international seminar in Beijing on November 16-17. The event, themed "Joint Efforts for Stable Development Amidst Global Changes and Uncertainty," included analysts from 18 Asian and European countries. Uzbekistan's representative highlighted reforms in democratization, digitalization, and governance.

item.title: Kazakhstan Climbs Eight Places in Global Innovation Index Ranking
item.description: Kazakhstan has improved its position by eight places in the 2026 Global Innovation Index, reaching 73rd out of 139 economies. The country ranks first in Central Asia and second among Central and South Asian economies. This marks Kazakhstan's best result in a decade, according to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

item.title: Uzbekistan Deputy Energy Minister Urges Shift to Alternative Fuels for Greenhouses
item.description: Uzbekistan's Deputy Energy Minister Umid Madaminov stated that natural gas reserves are diminishing. He urged greenhouse owners to switch to alternative fuels like propane-butane, pellets, or geothermal heating systems. This transition is necessary due to the declining production and reserves of natural gas in the country.

item.title: Kazakhstan Banks Offer Up to 18.6% Annual Yield on Deposits in Q3 2026
item.description: Kazakhstani banks offered average annual yields of up to 18.6% on certain deposit types in the third quarter of 2026. Despite a decrease in the National Bank's base rate, deposits are expected to remain attractive until year-end, according to a Kazakhstan Deposit Insurance Fund (KDIF) review.

item.title: Emilbek Zakirov Appointed Deputy Minister of Agriculture and Director of Water Resources Service
item.description: Emilbek Zakirov has been appointed Deputy Minister of Water Resources, Agriculture, and Processing Industry, and Director of the Water Resources Service in Kyrgyzstan. The appointment was made by the Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers, Adylbek Kasymaliev. Zakirov replaces Baktybek Anarkulov and previously worked as an expert in the Presidential Administration.

item.title: New Head of Samruk-Kazyna Fund to Be Appointed Soon, Says Prime Minister
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov announced that a new chairman for the Samruk-Kazyna Fund will be appointed shortly. He assured that the fund's operations, strategy, and investment projects will continue uninterrupted, with full continuity of management. Law enforcement is investigating specific officials, but the fund's overall activities are not in doubt. Financial obligations will be met.

item.title: Central Asian Universities Establish EU-Backed Renewable Energy Research Network
item.description: A new network for renewable energy research has launched in Astana, backed by the EU. It aims to study grid integration for solar and wind power and enhance regional energy system reliability. The network, part of the EURECA project, involves universities from Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, and Uzbekistan, with plans to include Kyrgyzstan and Turkmenistan soon.

item.title: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee Investigates $100,000 Road Repair Theft in Pavlodar Region
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee (KNB) is investigating the embezzlement of 45 million tenge (approximately $100,000) allocated for local road repairs in the Pavlodar region. Prosecutors discovered that the rural district administration illegally transferred the funds to a construction company for work that was not performed.

item.title: International Companies Involved in Almaty SuperSki Resort Construction
item.description: International firms specializing in cable car construction, ski resort design, and modern architecture are participating in the Almaty SuperSki mountain resort project. Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has set a target launch for December 2028. French company POMA has begun foundation work for cable cars, while Swiss Blumer–Lehmann will design building structures. Danish Bjarke Ingels Group is developing the mountain village concept.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Considers Mandating Online Coaches Disclose Education and Experience
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering a law that would require online coaches and course sellers to disclose their educational background, qualifications, and professional experience before receiving payment. Proposed amendments to consumer protection and advertising laws aim to ensure clients receive accurate information about online experts' credentials. This would apply to paid consultations, mentorship, and training programs offered online.

item.title: Kazakh Prime Minister Announces Change in Head of Samruk-Kazyna Fund
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov has announced a change in the leadership of the Samruk-Kazyna National Welfare Fund. Further details regarding the specific personnel change were not immediately provided in the initial report.

item.title: Uzbekistan Central Bank Launches New System for Salary Payments
item.description: Uzbekistan's Central Bank has introduced a new system allowing employees to receive salaries and bonuses on cards or e-wallets of their chosen banks, regardless of their employer's bank. This eliminates the need to open new accounts for salary projects, offering greater flexibility to workers. The system is initially for private companies but will expand later.

item.title: New Head and Enhanced Control: What Awaits Samruk-Kazyna
item.description: Kazakh Prime Minister Olzhas Bektenov stated that a new chairman will soon be appointed to Samruk-Kazyna, with a focus on strengthening corporate governance and internal controls. This comes amid an investigation into top management. The fund's operations and investment projects will continue as planned.

item.title: 231 People Died in Workplace Accidents in Uzbekistan Over 10 Months
item.description: Uzbekistan's State Labor Inspectorate reported that 231 people died as a result of workplace accidents during the first 10 months of the year. The report details the regions and sectors where the majority of these incidents occurred. Further details are available via the provided link.
